title: Distinguishedness for supplied left-derived values and maps
statement: In Situation 05S8 [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], let $(X,Y,Z,f,g,h)$ be a distinguished triangle [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Supply values $LX,LY,LZ$ of the denominator pro-diagrams, with natural cone maps $uX,uY,uZ$ and their retraction and common-stage certificates [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram]. Supply $lf:LX\to LY$ and $lg:LY\to LZ$ satisfying every first denominator-square equation of [lem-pur-derived-functor-morphisms-05sa] for $f$ and $g$. Then there exists $lh:LZ\to LX[1]$ such that $(LX,LY,LZ,lf,lg,lh)$ is distinguished and, for every denominator square (s followed by h equals h-prime followed by the shift of s-prime), one has $uZ_s\circ F(h\prime)=lh\circ uX_{s\prime}[1]\circ(F.commShiftIso(1))^{-1}_{s\prime.left}$. This is the shift identification of [lem-pur-derived-functor-shift-05su].

proof.text: Use the supplied values $A$ and $B$, their supplied retraction-certified cone maps $u^X_{s}:A\to F(X')$ over $S/X$ and $u^Y_{s'}:B\to F(Y')$ over $S/Y$, and let $LF(f):A\to B$ be the supplied map whose denominator-square equation is that of [lem-pur-derived-functor-morphisms-05sa], so that $u^Y_{s'}\circ LF(f)=F(f')\circ u^X_{s}$ whenever $f\circ s=s'\circ f'$. By [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram] choose an index $s'_0:Y'\to Y$ in $S/Y$ with a retraction $\beta:F(Y')\to B$ ($\beta\circ u^Y_{s'_0}=\mathrm{id}_B$) and an index $s_0:X_0\to X$ with a retraction $\alpha_0:F(X_0)\to A$. The second MS2 clause of [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], applied to $s'_0$ and $f\circ s_0$, gives $t_1:X_1\to X_0$ in $S$ and $f_1:X_1\to Y'$ with $f\circ s_0\circ t_1=s'_0\circ f_1$. Put $s_1=s_0\circ t_1$ and $\alpha_1=\alpha_0\circ F(t_1)$; then $\alpha_1\circ u^X_{s_1}=\alpha_0\circ u^X_{s_0}=\mathrm{id}_A$, and (using cofilteredness of $S/X$) $\alpha_1$ again satisfies the factorization clause of the definition at the index $s_1$. Applying that clause to $j=s_1$ and equalizing the two resulting arrows to $s_1$ in the cofiltered $S/X$, choose $t_2:X'\to X_1$ in $S$ with $F(t_2)=u^X_{s_1}\circ\alpha_1\circ F(t_2)$. Put $s=s_1\circ t_2:X'\to X$, $f'=f_1\circ t_2:X'\to Y'$ and $\alpha=\alpha_1\circ F(t_2):F(X')\to A$. Then $f\circ s=s'_0\circ f'$, $\alpha\circ u^X_{s}=\alpha_1\circ u^X_{s_1}=\mathrm{id}_A$, and $\beta\circ F(f')=\beta\circ F(f_1)\circ u^X_{s_1}\circ\alpha_1\circ F(t_2)=\beta\circ u^Y_{s'_0}\circ LF(f)\circ\alpha=LF(f)\circ\alpha$ by the cone square of [lem-pur-derived-functor-morphisms-05sa] for $f\circ s_1=s'_0\circ f_1$. Complete $f'$ to a distinguished triangle $(X',Y',Z',f',g',h')$ (TR1); MS6 (in the form stated in [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], with source triangle $(X',Y',Z')$ and target $(X,Y,Z)$) gives $t:Z'\to Z$ in $S$ making $(s,s'_0,t)$ a morphism of triangles. Choose a distinguished triangle $(A,B,C,LF(f),b,c)$ (TR1). Since $F$ is exact, $(F(X'),F(Y'),F(Z'),F(f'),F(g'),F(h'))$ is distinguished, and TR3 extends $(\alpha,\beta)$ to a morphism of triangles $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ into $(A,B,C,LF(f),b,c)$, with $\gamma:F(Z')\to C$ (the last square read through $F(X'[1])\cong F(X')[1]$).

source.place: Lemma 05SC proof, paragraphs 1--3, dualized to pro-objects over S/X, S/Y

proof.text: Let $\mathcal I$ be the category of [lem-pur-triangle-morphism-category-05r9] for $(X,Y,Z,f,g,h)$: triangle morphisms into $(X,Y,Z)$ with components in $S$. It is cofiltered, $j_0=((X',Y',Z'),(s,s'_0,t))$ is one of its objects, and its projections to $S/X$, $S/Y$, $S/Z$ are initial. By [lem-pur-essential-constant-cofinal-0a1s], $F(X'')$ and $F(Y'')$ over $\mathcal I$ are essentially constant with values $A$, $B$ and the restricted cone maps $u^X$, $u^Y$; and it suffices to show that $F(Z'')$ over $\mathcal I$ is essentially constant with value $C$, for then the pro-object over $S/Z$ is essentially constant with value $C$, i.e. $LF$ is defined at $Z$ with value $C$.

source.place: Lemma 05SC proof, paragraph beginning 'Consider the category I', dual form

proof.text: Fix an object $W$ of $\mathcal D'$. For each object of $\mathcal I$, $\operatorname{Hom}(-,W)$ applied to the distinguished triangle $F(X'')\to F(Y'')\to F(Z'')\to F(X'')[1]$ gives an exact sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(F(Y'')[1],W)\to\operatorname{Hom}(F(X'')[1],W)\to\operatorname{Hom}(F(Z''),W)\to\operatorname{Hom}(F(Y''),W)\to\operatorname{Hom}(F(X''),W)$, functorial over $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}$ (filtered, as $\mathcal I$ is cofiltered); its colimit over $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact]. Map the sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(B[1],W)\to\operatorname{Hom}(A[1],W)\to\operatorname{Hom}(C,W)\to\operatorname{Hom}(B,W)\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,W)$ to it by $\varphi\mapsto$ the class at $j_0$ of $\varphi$ composed with $\beta[1],\alpha[1],\gamma,\beta,\alpha$; the squares commute because $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ is a morphism of triangles. The map $\operatorname{Hom}(A,W)\to\varinjlim\operatorname{Hom}(F(X''),W)$ is bijective: its composite with the bijection $\varinjlim\operatorname{Hom}(F(X''),W)\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,W)$ given by the cone $u^X$ ([lem-pc-essentially-constant-pro-hom-colimit]) is $\varphi\mapsto\varphi\circ\alpha\circ u^X_{s}=\varphi$; likewise for $B$ with $\beta$. The shifted positions are the same statements for $W[-1]$, since $[1]$ is an automorphism of $\mathcal D'$ (no derived value of a shift is involved). The five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] shows that $\operatorname{Hom}(C,W)\to\varinjlim_{\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Hom}(F(Z''),W)$, $\varphi\mapsto[\varphi\circ\gamma]_{j_0}$, is bijective.

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-essential-constant-pro-criterion-05py] and [lem-pur-essential-constant-cofinal-0a1s] to construct a cone with value C at Z. The Hom-colimit comparison [lem-pc-essentially-constant-pro-hom-colimit] for this cone and the supplied cone at LZ gives an isomorphism C to LZ compatible with all legs. The triangle-morphism square for b and the uniqueness clause of [lem-pur-derived-functor-morphisms-05sa] identify b followed by this isomorphism with the supplied lg. Define lh by its inverse followed by c. The third square, through the canonical comparison of [lem-pur-derived-functor-shift-05su], gives the shifted cone equation for every denominator square of h; its target leg is the shift of uX followed by the inverse commShiftIso. Transport the distinguished triangle (A,B,C) along this isomorphism at the third vertex by [def-weil-triangulated-category].

theorem leftDerived_value_triangle_extension
    {C : Type u} {D : Type uD} [Category.{v} C] [Category.{vD} D]
    [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ] [Preadditive C]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C]
    [CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated C]
    [HasZeroObject D] [HasShift D ℤ] [Preadditive D]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D]
    [CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated D]
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated]
    (S : MorphismProperty C)
    (hS : S.IsSaturatedTriangulatedMultiplicativeSystem)
    (T : Triangle C) (hT : T ∈ distTriang C)
    (LX LY LZ : D)
    (hX : F.IsTriangulatedLeftDerivedValue S hS T.obj₁ LX)
    (hY : F.IsTriangulatedLeftDerivedValue S hS T.obj₂ LY)
    (hZ : F.IsTriangulatedLeftDerivedValue S hS T.obj₃ LZ)
    (uX : (Functor.const (S.Over ⊤ T.obj₁)).obj LX ⟶
      MorphismProperty.Over.forget S ⊤ T.obj₁ ⋙ Over.forget T.obj₁ ⋙ F)
    (uY : (Functor.const (S.Over ⊤ T.obj₂)).obj LY ⟶
      MorphismProperty.Over.forget S ⊤ T.obj₂ ⋙ Over.forget T.obj₂ ⋙ F)
    (uZ : (Functor.const (S.Over ⊤ T.obj₃)).obj LZ ⟶
      MorphismProperty.Over.forget S ⊤ T.obj₃ ⋙ Over.forget T.obj₃ ⋙ F)
    (huX : ∃ s₀ : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₁, ∃ r : F.obj s₀.left ⟶ LX,
      uX.app s₀ ≫ r = 𝟙 LX ∧
        ∀ s : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₁, ∃ t : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₁,
          ∃ a : t ⟶ s₀, ∃ b : t ⟶ s,
            F.map b.left = F.map a.left ≫ r ≫ uX.app s)
    (huY : ∃ s₀ : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₂, ∃ r : F.obj s₀.left ⟶ LY,
      uY.app s₀ ≫ r = 𝟙 LY ∧
        ∀ s : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₂, ∃ t : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₂,
          ∃ a : t ⟶ s₀, ∃ b : t ⟶ s,
            F.map b.left = F.map a.left ≫ r ≫ uY.app s)
    (huZ : ∃ s₀ : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₃, ∃ r : F.obj s₀.left ⟶ LZ,
      uZ.app s₀ ≫ r = 𝟙 LZ ∧
        ∀ s : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₃, ∃ t : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₃,
          ∃ a : t ⟶ s₀, ∃ b : t ⟶ s,
            F.map b.left = F.map a.left ≫ r ≫ uZ.app s)
    (lf : LX ⟶ LY) (lg : LY ⟶ LZ)
    (hf : ∀ (s : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₁) (s' : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₂)
        (f' : s.left ⟶ s'.left),
        s.hom ≫ T.mor₁ = f' ≫ s'.hom →
          uX.app s ≫ F.map f' = lf ≫ uY.app s')
    (hg : ∀ (s : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₂) (s' : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₃)
        (g' : s.left ⟶ s'.left),
        s.hom ≫ T.mor₂ = g' ≫ s'.hom →
          uY.app s ≫ F.map g' = lg ≫ uZ.app s')
    : ∃ lh : LZ ⟶ (shiftFunctor D (1 : ℤ)).obj LX,
      (∀ (s : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₃) (s' : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₁)
        (h' : s.left ⟶ (shiftFunctor C (1 : ℤ)).obj s'.left),
        s.hom ≫ T.mor₃ = h' ≫ (shiftFunctor C (1 : ℤ)).map s'.hom →
          uZ.app s ≫ F.map h' =
            lh ≫ (shiftFunctor D (1 : ℤ)).map (uX.app s') ≫
              (F.commShiftIso (1 : ℤ)).inv.app s'.left) ∧
      Triangle.mk lf lg lh ∈ distTriang D
